stem: A 15-year-old girl living with HIV, on antiretroviral therapy for several years, presents with about seven weeks of cough and worsening fatigue, which she and her family attributed to a demanding harvest season. Her most recent CD4 count, checked two months ago, was 310 cells/uL. No known TB contact in the household. No prior TB treatment, no known drug-resistant contact. Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF positive, rifampicin not detected. Exam: thin, mild bilateral crackles, no lymphadenopathy.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents in a rural household; living with HIV, on ART, followed at a local clinic
patient.presenting_complaint: Cough and worsening fatigue, attributed initially to harvest workload
patient.exam_findings: Thin, mild bilateral crackles, no lymphadenopathy
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; on established antiretroviral therapy; no prior TB treatment

distractors: Fatigue attributed to the demands of harvest season rather than a new, superimposed infectious process
Her relatively preserved CD4 count (310 cells/uL) taken as reassuring against opportunistic infection risk
Cough attributed to dust exposure during fieldwork rather than investigated as a distinct process
ntep_correct_actions: Give cotrimoxazole preventive therapy to this patient regardless of her CD4 count, since she is HIV-positive with active TB.
Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
who_correct_actions: Give cotrimoxazole preventive therapy to this patient regardless of her CD4 count, since she is HIV-positive with active TB.
Perform rifampicin-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen regardless of prior treatment history, birth/residence history, contact history, or HIV status.
us_correct_actions: Reserve cotrimoxazole preventive therapy primarily for HIV-infected TB patients with a CD4 count below 200 cells/uL; at her CD4 of 310 cells/uL, this framework would not routinely use it.

Order rapid rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient because her HIV-positive status independently meets one of the specific risk criteria this framework uses to decide who receives testing -- not because testing is a universal policy.
critical_error_conditions: Omitting rifampicin-resistance testing for this patient despite her established TB diagnosis
expected_divergence_points: Whether cotrimoxazole preventive therapy is given to all HIV-positive TB patients regardless of CD4 count or reserved for those with CD4 below 200 cells/uL
Whether rifampicin-resistance testing is performed as a matter of universal policy or because specific risk criteria (in this case, her HIV status) are met
